sections.quote: They were very friendly and knowledgeable. I had a sewer backup and my basement and they explained detail by detail of why it was happening.

sections.heading: A Floor Drain Backing Up, a Tub That Gurgles
body: Tell us what you're seeing: a floor drain backing up, a tub that gurgles when the washer runs, a smell, or water that won't leave the lowest drain in the house.

sections.heading: A Sunday Septic Backup, Found and Priced
body: Noel S. had been in his house for only a month when the downstairs shower backed up and flooded the bathroom and part of the basement. It was a weekend, and he wrote that JM was the only company that answered his request for emergency help.

The crew came out on a Sunday and found that roots had infiltrated the line. He wrote that the price was less than he imagined, that they gave him advice and tips to prevent the damage, and that they recommended replacing the damaged line.

sections.quote: Jaime and his crew were practically immediate in their response to my sewer line needing to be cleared and partially replaced. They were friendly, completely professional, and what I appreciated most was their excellent communication and keeping me apprised of the work and my options every step of the way.
sections.name: Jay P.

sections.heading: Months of Backups, Then a Cleanout
body: Justice W. had backup problems for months with no cleanout. JM came out and installed one quickly, at what she called a very affordable price. She wrote that it was such a stress relief.
Stuart I. had sewer backing up into his basement floor drain. The crew fixed the problem and cleaned up when they were done.
Carol J. called about a floor drain. Jaime came out to look and found the issue immediately, came out on a weekend day to fix it, and did it quickly.

sections.heading: A Collapsed Line, a Day and a Half, and the Patio Put Back
body: Katherine B. had JM replace a collapsed line. The job took about a day and a half, and the crew talked with her and her husband about what was going on and explained what they would be doing.
Getting to the pipe meant breaking up their concrete patio. The crew managed to put it back together to the best of their abilities. She named Tanner, Zeb, Saul and Jaime as fantastic at their jobs.

sections.heading: A Late-Night Clog, and a Return Visit
body: William W. called many companies late at night about a main line drain clog, and wrote that he was happy to get an answer from a very nice dispatcher. The tech was there within the time frame, and the price was reasonable.

The next morning the tech returned to put the correct size wax ring back on the toilet. Lili S. had a sewer backup in mid-December, and wrote that JM was on time, professional, friendly, fairly priced and knowledgeable.

sections.heading: New Lines and Cleanouts, on Different Occasions
body: Angela L. wrote that JM fixed her sewer line, and that they have done cleanouts and added new lines for her on different occasions.
Sarah V. had a problem with her sewer line. The crew responded promptly and replaced it, and she wrote that they did an exceptional job.

sections.heading: Floor Drain Backing Up? Your Questions

items.q: Is it the sewer line or just a drain?
items.a: Call and describe it: which drains are slow, which are backing up, and since when. We'll tell you what we think.

items.q: Do you clear lines and replace them?
items.a: Sewer line clearing, cleanouts and new lines all come up in customer reviews. Call (316) 491-3612 and tell us what is backing up.

items.q: Will you dig up my yard?
items.a: That depends on where the line is. Tell us what's above it when you call: a patio, a driveway, a tree, a flowerbed.

items.q: Can a cleanout be added to my line?
items.a: Ask when you call whether one makes sense on your line.

items.q: How long will a sewer job take?
items.a: It depends on the line and what's above it. Ask when you call.

items.q: Do you come out for a floor drain?
items.a: Yes. Carol J. called about hers, and Jaime came out on a weekend day to fix it. Call (316) 491-3612 and tell us which drain it is.

items.q: Will you clean up when the job is done?
items.a: Stuart I. and Dean B. both wrote that the crew cleaned up after the work. Katherine B.'s crew even put her concrete patio back together after breaking it up to reach the pipe.

items.q: Do you take weekend sewer calls?
items.a: Call (316) 491-3612 and ask. Noel S. wrote that JM answered his weekend emergency request and came out on a Sunday.

sections.heading: A Hot Water Tank Replaced, and a Church Opening the Next Day
body: Rachel M. had her hot water tank replaced. She wrote that the crew was very polite, quoted the price upfront and was very efficient, and that she will be calling for all her future plumbing needs.

Melpha S. needed repairs and a water heater installed in a newly leased property her church had gotten. Jaime made suggestions on what work needed to be done in the building, and was able to get the job done before opening day, which was the next day.

sections.heading: Read Us the Label on the Tank
body: Tell us how old the heater is, if you know, and whether it runs on gas or electric. Tell us whether it's leaking and where, and whether the water is hot at all.
If you can read the label on the side of the tank, read us what it says.

sections.heading: No Water, a New Line, a Repiped House, and a New Heater
body: Carol H. was without water. Jaime came out the day she called and clearly communicated the issue. His team installed a new water service line, repiped the entire house and installed a new water heater, and also repaired a slow draining lavatory. The work was finished in two days.

sections.heading: A New Tank With a Sticker On It
body: Dustin C. had JM replace the water heater and fix up the old sump pump. He wrote that the team was professional and responsive, and that they tagged his new tank with a memorable sticker.

sections.heading: Cold Shower? Your Questions

items.q: Should I repair or replace my water heater?
items.a: Both are on our list. Tell us how old the heater is, what it is doing and whether it leaks.

items.q: Do you repair water heaters too?
items.a: Yes. Water heater repair is on our list.

items.q: What should I do if my water heater is leaking?
items.a: Shut off the water supply to the heater, and the power or gas if you can reach them safely, then call us. Don't wait for it to drain on its own.

items.q: Will you tell me the price before you start?
items.a: You hear your options and the price before we start.

items.q: How fast can a heater be replaced?
items.a: David C.'s new heater was installed and working within four hours of his call. Every house is different, so ask when you call.

items.q: What do I do while I wait for you?
items.a: Keep the supply to the heater shut off if it is leaking, and keep your phone nearby so we can reach you.

items.q: Do you install heaters in buildings other than houses?
items.a: Melpha S. had a water heater installed in a newly leased property that her church had gotten. Call (316) 491-3612 and tell us about the building.

items.q: What if the heater is part of a bigger plumbing problem?
items.a: Carol H. had no water at all, and her new water heater was one part of the job. Tell us everything that is going wrong when you call, not only the heater.

items.q: Do you fix other plumbing while you are there?
items.a: Dustin C. had his water heater replaced and the old sump pump fixed up in the same visit. Tell us everything that needs a look when you call.

items.q: What if the heater goes out on a weekend?
items.a: Call (316) 491-3612 and ask when we can come. David C. called after his heater went out on a Friday night, and Jaime came on Saturday, within two hours after the call.

items.q: Does it matter whether my heater is gas or electric?
items.a: Tell us which it is when you call, along with how old it is and what the label on the tank says.

lead.heading: Why we led with explaining what's wrong
lead.text: The scariest moment for a Wichita homeowner is the water off and a stranger at the door, and right behind it is not knowing whether the repair is real. We led with explaining what's wrong and why because it is built on things Google can't find anywhere else: what your customers say about how you explain, and Wichita details like a floor drain, a collapsed line and a Sunday faucet. That is also why it can help you rank.
